# How Do You Find a Particle With No Charge?

<!-- STEP id="quiet" -->
## Charged Plates Do Nothing

Electrons and protons were discovered by bending them between charged plates. A neutron has no charge, so charged plates do not bend it at all. It can only be noticed by what it hits.

<!-- STEP id="wax" -->
## An Invisible Ray Hits Wax

When alpha particles struck the metal beryllium, it gave out an invisible ray. When that ray hit a block of wax, protons flew out of the wax at high speed. Wax is rich in hydrogen, and the nucleus of a hydrogen atom is a single proton.

Irene and Frederic Joliot-Curie saw this first, and they thought the ray was a kind of light.

<!-- STEP id="mass" -->
## A Ray With No Mass Could Not Hit That Hard

Their idea was reasonable, but light has no mass, and the protons were moving much too fast. Think of a carrom board: the heavy striker sends a coin flying, but a ball of paper hardly moves it. Try it here by changing the mass of the hidden particle.

<!-- STEP id="takeaway" -->
**Chadwick concluded that the ray is a stream of neutral particles, each about as heavy as a proton. These are neutrons.**

Without a charge, the neutron can only be found by what it hits, and that is why it was found so long after the proton.
